_doc: Phase-81b surface-recall lens taxonomy (RESEARCH-ONLY, un-wired). GENERIC vocab only — NO subject-specific identifiers. A surface class is a SECURITY-RELEVANT ENTRYPOINT SHAPE, not a bug. The lens is recall-biased: any in-scope public/external function (+ receive/fallback) matching >=1 class becomes a STATIC_LEAD with mechanism left uncertain; precision is the downstream P77/P78 job.

bridge_receive.why: inbound bridge/cross-chain callback that EXECUTES on an attacker-influenced payload from a relayer (state-changing, not a view/math helper). P81c: tightened to a real bridge-callback NAME or a cross-chain SHAPE; abi.decode/bare-bytes no longer trigger it.

external_executor.why: executes/forwards an arbitrary target+data call supplied (directly or indirectly) by the caller

admin_config_setter.why: authority-boundary mutation of routing/ownership/oracle/fee config. P81f: NO LONGER requires an auth modifier — an UNGUARDED state-changing config setter (the missing-access-control bug class, e.g. H-01 unguarded setRouter) is exactly the interesting case and must be captured. The signals.auth_gated flag distinguishes guarded vs unguarded downstream; exclude_view_pure keeps view 'set'-named getters out.

refund_path.why: refund / leftover / excess / sweep return of residual value

value_exit.why: moves value out of the contract (possibly to a caller-controlled recipient)

calldata_forward.why: user-controlled bytes payload forwarded into an external/low-level call

auth_boundary.why: trusted-caller / role / owner gate (or an UNGATED state-changing entry, which is itself the interesting case)

_no_subject_names_note: This file MUST NOT contain any subject-specific contract/function identifier (asserted by tests). All tokens above are generic DeFi/bridge vocabulary or standard protocol-callback names (sgReceive/lzReceive are Stargate/LayerZero interface methods, not subject-specific).
